page: Microsoft Azure F80als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 80 dedicated physical cores and 80 vCPUs running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 160 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The configuration includes no onboard local storage, relying on external network-attached storage solutions, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark assessments show top-tier execution across raw compute and memory throughput metrics. The instance registered a multi-core score of 290,605.12 and a single-core score of 3,780.35 in stress-ng evaluations, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 128,254.89. Uncached large-block read operations achieved 477.47 GB/sec, while write operations reached 213.01 GB/sec. Instruction support features AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16, accelerating cryptographic operations, matrix math, and vectorized arithmetic. Data processing benchmarks demonstrated high throughput, including 1,069.61 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 199.48 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation delivers high compute density for organizations seeking CPU-focused throughput without the cost overhead of unutilized system RAM. However, the lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires all persistent and scratch I/O to traverse network storage infrastructure, which impacts workloads dependent on ultralow storage latency.

Microsoft Azure F80als_v7 is suitable for compute-heavy workloads that operate comfortably within a 2 GB per core memory footprint. Appropriate applications include parallel batch processing, continuous integration and build compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, and CPU-based machine learning inference routines.

Configured with 160 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators and local scratch disks are absent, requiring external storage integration. In performance testing, the instance placed in the top tier for stress-ng compute tasks, uncached memory bandwidth reaching 477.47 GB/sec reads, and Redis operations scaling to 199.48 million SET ops per second. The lack of hyperthreading contention ensures stable instruction throughput, aided by AVX-512 and bfloat16 instruction sets. F80als_v7 is targeted at CPU-bound deployments such as automated build pipelines, batch compute workloads, web serving, and CPU inference that require high core counts without expansive memory allocations.
